question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

He is looking forward **to meet you soon.**
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. to meeting you soon .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"looking forward to"** is always followed by a gerund (**verb + ing**), not an infinitive verb (**to + verb**).
 
• In the given sentence, **"to meet"** is incorrect because it uses the infinitive form of the verb.
 
• The correct structure is **"looking forward to meeting"**, where **"meeting"** is the gerund form.

Correct sentence: *He is looking forward to **meeting** you soon.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common phrases followed by gerunds:**
 
 
• **"looking forward to"** + gerund (e.g., meeting, seeing).
 
• **"be used to"** + gerund (e.g., working, studying).
 
• **"be interested in"** + gerund (e.g., learning, exploring).
 
 
 
• **Common phrases followed by infinitives:**
 
 
• **"want to"** + infinitive (e.g., meet, see).
 
• **"decide to"** + infinitive (e.g., go, leave).
 
• **"hope to"** + infinitive (e.g., achieve, succeed).
